locus_mapping.method: UniProt ordered locus name (MMAR_xxxx) -> RefSeq /old_locus_tag on gene features -> RefSeq /locus_tag (MMAR_RSxxxxx)

method.ontologies: BP, MF and CC tested separately
method.propagation: true-path rule over is_a and part_of, within namespace
method.universe: genes in the gene set's background with at least one annotation in the ontology being tested

backgrounds.tested_<contrast>: genes with non-missing DESeq2 padj in that contrast
backgrounds.tested_both_simulators: genes with non-missing padj in both clinostat_vs_static1g and rpm2_vs_static1g
backgrounds.wgcna_all_genes: every gene in wgcna_module_assignments.tsv, grey included

method.deg_definition: DESeq2 padj < 0.05, direction by sign of log2FoldChange
method.term_size_definition: annotated universe genes in the term (after propagation)
method.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg within each gene set and ontology, over all size-eligible terms (zero-overlap terms enter with p = 1)
method.multiple_testing_sensitivity: fdr_bh_hit_terms_only: BH over terms with at least one overlapping gene (clusterProfiler enricher convention); reported only, not used for calls
method.evidence_codes: all UniProtKB GO evidence codes kept, IEA included
method.small_set_flag: gene sets with fewer than 10 GO-annotated genes

tested_clinostat_vs_static1g, tested_rpm2_vs_static1g, tested_clinostat_vs_rpm2, tested_both_simulators: 2821 of 3967 genes (71.1%) have at least one GO annotation (BP 1494, MF 2432, CC 1438). Unannotated genes, mostly hypothetical proteins, cannot contribute.
wgcna_all_genes: 2822 of 3968 genes (71.1%) have at least one GO annotation (BP 1494, MF 2433, CC 1439). Unannotated genes, mostly hypothetical proteins, cannot contribute.

BH is applied over all size-eligible terms (conservative). With the clusterProfiler enricher convention (BH over terms with at least one hit, column fdr_bh_hit_terms_only) the total across gene sets is 291 significant term-tests instead of 201.
GO terms overlap (parents and children share genes), so significant terms within a gene set are not independent findings.

The hypergeometric test treats genes as independent. Co-transcribed operons whose members share annotations (for example nuo or mce clusters) can drive a term on their own; check overlap_gene_ids before interpreting a term.
